title: Eton Mess
subtitle: Crushed meringue, whipped cream, and strawberries
excerpt: A glorious, effortless combination of broken meringue, softly whipped cream, and fresh strawberries macerated in a little sugar. The easiest and most rewarding British summer dessert.

recipe.sourceNotes: Eton Mess is a British dessert traditionally served at the annual cricket match between Eton College and Harrow School at Lord's Cricket Ground. The earliest written record appears in an Eton College cookbook published in 1893. The name mess refers to the casual, tumbled appearance of the finished dish: broken meringue mixed with whipped cream and strawberries. The dish is said to have originally contained either strawberries or bananas, and the meringue may have been an accident (a Labrador sat on the dessert, according to one account). Whatever its origins, the combination of crisp-chewy meringue, soft cream, and sharp berries is one of the most reliably successful in British pudding cooking. The meringue can be bought ready-made or homemade; the rest of the dish requires no cooking and can be assembled in minutes.

content.text: The strawberries should be macerated with a little sugar for at least 30 minutes: the sugar draws out the juice and the berries become sweeter and slightly softened, which integrates them better with the cream and meringue. A few tablespoons of the strawberry juice stirred through the cream turns it a pretty pale pink. Assemble at the last moment: if it sits too long the meringue softens completely and the dish loses its textural contrast.

content.text: Mix the strawberries with the caster sugar in a bowl. Leave to macerate for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally. The strawberries will release their juice and become slightly softened.
Whip the double cream with the icing sugar and vanilla to soft peaks. Stir a few tablespoons of the strawberry juice through the cream.

If making the meringue from scratch, whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, then gradually whisk in the caster sugar until thick and glossy. Spoon onto a lined baking tray and bake at 120 C / fan 100 C for 90 minutes. Cool completely. Break the meringue into rough pieces. Fold the meringue and most of the strawberries through the cream, leaving some strawberries and their juices to spoon over the top. Serve at once in glasses or a large bowl.
